Alice Morris: Kicking off a quick sync on the merchant pilot — they want BYO KMS with HSM-backed keys + a clear acceptance criteria list and billing cadence. Who can own the tech presales scope?
Ben Liu: I can take the tech lead for the POC. Need to confirm network topology and egress constraints from their infra team.
Carla Singh: +1 Ben. Also we should clarify whether they expect CMK in CloudHSM or an on-prem HSM via proxy. That affects latency / key op cost.
Alice Morris: They told Sales they have a managed HSM cluster (on-prem) and want our connector to call it. Contractually they want key custody proof + attestation doc.
Dave Ortega: For attestation we can provide an HSM attestation checklist and recent ATE report. I can assemble the docs but need the exact model (Thales vs AWS CloudHSM) and whether they require FIPS 140-2 vs 140-3.
Emma Patel: Legal wants the acceptance criteria in the SOW. Please include: successful end-to-end encrypt/decrypt with BYO keys, key rotation test, audit log export, and no data exfil observed during the window.
Ben Liu: Proposed technical acceptance tests: 1) End-to-end sign/encrypt with their CMK for 10k sample requests at target QPS. 2) Rotation exercise: perform a rotation and verify 0% failed decrypts after cutover. 3) Latency SLOs: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms for key-op-invocations. 4) Audit log ingestion to their SIEM within 60s.
Carla Singh: For the rotation test, suggest a staged handoff (canary + full) — we'll run this sequence:
```
# rotation-playbook (simplified)
1. push new key version to HSM (custodian)
2. set read-preferred to new key on canary instances (5%)
3. validate canary for 30m (errors < 0.1%)
4. promote to 100% and monitor for 1h
```
Carla Singh: We should include rollback criteria (error spike > 1% or p95 breach).
Dave Ortega: Security question: how will we handle key compromise simulations? We need a backstop plan for emergency revocation and replay protection. I can draft runbook language.
Alice Morris: Pricing — they asked about proration for pilot months and any fees for BYO KMS connector. Should present both Hosted API + Dedicated reserve options.
Ben Liu: Pricing notes: connector engineering is included in enterprise onboarding up to 10 days; beyond that we bill T&M. For Dedicated, we need to quote reserved GPU capacity + optional higher retention for logs. For hosted, per-key ops adds marginal cost due to HSM egress.
Emma Patel: For SOW clarity: call out connector scope (networking, IP allowlist, cert exchange), runbook deliverables, acceptance window (14 days), and billing: pilot invoice at start for minimum reserved commit (prorated) + engineering hours post-pilot if out of scope.
Alice Morris: Customer asked whether key rotation can be customer-scheduled vs our automated rotation. They want customer control for compliance.
Carla Singh: We support both. For BYO keys we can expose a rotation webhook they call, or we can run rotation via their Ops account. Document required IAM roles and API tokens.
Ben Liu: Action items: @Dave to attach attestation checklist + compromise runbook; @Emma to draft SOW snippets for acceptance and billing; @Carla to produce connector network requirements; I'll assemble POC test harness and perf script.
Dave Ortega: I'll drop the attestation template and a short runbook in the thread by EOD.
Emma Patel: I'll draft the SOW language and send a redline by tomorrow morning.
Carla Singh: I'll post the minimal firewall + cert exchange steps and an example IP list.

Alice Morris: Thanks team. I'll update the customer with proposed acceptance criteria and tentative pricing. Ping here with any updates. :thumbsup:
